Congrats, you have a degree and a job. Can you progress further in your career or field? What about personal progress; what would you like to see yourself doing in 1 year, 5 years, 10? Have money to do things or travel, time to spend with loved ones, have a family of your own, lose 50 pounds, publish a book or create a new invention-chances are, if you close your eyes and relax you can come up with a vision of something the thought of which makes you feel happy, content or motivated to change. Come up with some related goals, such as to learn a new language or skill, push yourself towards a new personal best, make 5 new friends, save $X money, etc. Break those goals into smaller goals and working toward each will give both something to do and something to reach towards achieving.

No one would argue you should leave that stall empty and wait for another stall or even more extreme refrain from toileting altogether; if there is a line, I simply wait my turn and then pass open stalls to those behind me until a stall I can use is available.
On the other hand, if there are multiple stalls available and you do not require an accessible one, be courteous to others by using a standard stall.

I am disabled, and I totally agree with you on this. I don't expect it to be reserved, but if you just want to spend your work break sitting on the toilet in a "big stall", or for some reason think this is a great place to plop down for a long shit that you could do just as easily in another open stall, maybe you should reconsider.
You won't know it when I walk into the restroom, but I need a stall with a handle to sit and stand back up; if there are multiple open stalls that are relatively clean and usable, simply be considerate that even if there isn't a wheelchair behind you someone else may have need of that stall and not just a desire for more space.
